correctness.rationale: Pair-interval saturation of a finite grid produces the full min–max box; any purported larger pseudo-intent would be pair-interval closed and hence already closed. Nonclosed pairs force distinct nontrivial premises in every complete sound basis, proving exact global rule minimum. A minimal-support argument shows each target box point needs at most d seeds for d≥2; balanced pair-box merging takes at most ceil(log2 d) rounds; the unit-vector witness forces that many by binary inference support size. One-dimensional cases handled separately. Independent finite exhaustive pseudo-intent and closure check in verify.py passed.
